officialDocs.label: API requests, headers and rate limits

verdict.summary: There is no self-serve developer console: you get a client_id and client_secret by emailing partners@copper.com with your app name, purpose and HTTPS callback, and after that there is no app review and a single all-access scope. The catch on the customer side is that third-party guides report the Developer API only works on Copper's Professional and Business plans, so Basic and trial accounts can't connect.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: The coding work is a few hours (authorization code flow, non-expiring token). The wait is for Copper's partners team to reply with credentials, and Copper publishes no turnaround time. Testing also needs a Copper account on a plan with API access.

timeToProd.assumes: A multi-tenant agent that reads and writes CRM records via OAuth; there's no separate production review, so production is ready once the partners team issues credentials.
timeToProd.waitingOn: Copper's partners team issuing OAuth credentials (no published SLA). No app review afterwards, but each customer needs a Professional or Business plan.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: The docs describe no approval step after registration. The range is our estimate of a manual email-based registration.

verdict.cost: No developer fee mentioned. End users reportedly need Copper Professional ($59/seat/mo annual) or Business ($99/seat/mo annual) for API access; Basic is excluded per third-party integration docs.

prerequisites.item: OAuth credentials issued by Copper (email partners@copper.com)
prerequisites.why: Copper's docs say to register your application by contacting them with its name, purpose and an HTTPS callback URL. They then issue the client_id and client_secret.

prerequisites.item: An HTTPS redirect_uri that accepts POST requests
prerequisites.why: Copper sends the user back to your redirect_uri with a POST (form-encoded) rather than the usual GET with query parameters.

prerequisites.item: A Copper account on a plan with Developer API access for testing (reportedly Professional or Business)
prerequisites.why: Third-party integration docs report that Basic and trial accounts get 'Developer API is not enabled for this account'.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: Copper's pricing page lists 'API & Embedded integration SDK' in the feature table, but the per-plan checkmarks weren't readable. The plan restriction comes from JustCall and n8n docs.

scopeTiers.impact: Grants read and modify access to the authenticated user's records (leads, people, companies, opportunities, tasks, activities, webhooks). It's backward compatible with legacy API keys. You can't request read-only access.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Copper says more granular scopes will be added in the future.

scopeTiers.impact: A Copper Admin generates a key in Settings and pastes it into your agent. No partner registration is needed, but it's a per-customer manual setup that Copper positions for individual users, while OAuth is preferred for partner integrations.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Only Admin users can generate API keys.

steps.title: Get a Copper account with API access
steps.detail: Sign up for or use a Copper account on a plan that includes the Developer API (reportedly Professional or Business), so you can test end to end.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: The plan requirement comes from third-party docs.

steps.title: Draft the registration request
steps.detail: Write the email to partners@copper.com with the app name, what the agent does with Copper data, and the HTTPS callback URL (production, plus a staging URL if you want one).

steps.title: Send the request to Copper's partners team
steps.detail: Email partners@copper.com from your company address and answer any follow-up questions.

steps.title: Wait for client_id and client_secret
steps.detail: Copper issues the credentials manually. No turnaround time is published.

steps.title: Handle the POST callback
steps.detail: Accept a form-encoded POST at the redirect_uri. Read code (or error) and state from the body, not the query string. Exempt this route from CSRF middleware that blocks cross-site POSTs, and verify state yourself.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The CSRF-middleware advice is our inference from the POST redirect.

steps.title: Exchange the code for a token
steps.detail: POST https://app.copper.com/oauth/token (form-encoded) with grant_type=authorization_code, code, redirect_uri, client_id and client_secret. Store the Bearer access_token encrypted per user. There's no refresh token.

steps.title: Call the API and respect limits
steps.detail: Call https://api.copper.com/developer_api/v1/... with Authorization: Bearer <token>. Throttle to 180 requests/min overall and 3 requests/sec on bulk endpoints, and back off on 429. Use webhooks subscriptions instead of polling where possible.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The OAuth flow page shows the Bearer header. The base URL comes from the 2021 domain-change changelog entry.

steps.title: Handle revocation
steps.detail: Users and admins can revoke your app under Settings > Integrations > Active Integrations. Treat a 401 as revoked and prompt the user to reconnect.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Mapping 401 to a revoked token is our inference.

steps.title: Go live
steps.detail: Turn on the Connect Copper button for customers. No Copper review is documented. If you want a listing in Copper's integrations directory, ask the partners team; that's optional for OAuth to work.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: The docs don't mention a marketplace listing process.

blockers.symptom: No developer console exists to create an OAuth app
blockers.cause: Copper registers OAuth clients manually through its partners team.
blockers.fix: Email partners@copper.com with your app name, purpose and HTTPS callback URL.

blockers.symptom: "Developer API is not enabled for this account"
blockers.cause: The customer's Copper account is on Basic or a trial plan without Developer API access.
blockers.fix: The customer upgrades to Professional or Business. Show a clear message before the OAuth step.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: The error string and plan mapping come from JustCall's troubleshooting guide, not Copper's docs.

blockers.symptom: Callback receives no code in the query string, or returns 403/419 from your framework
blockers.cause: Copper redirects with a POST and puts code in the form body. CSRF protection on the route can reject the cross-site POST.
blockers.fix: Read code and state from the POST body, and exempt the callback route from CSRF middleware while still checking state.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The framework rejection is our inference.

blockers.cause: More than 180 requests per minute, or more than 3 requests per second on bulk APIs.
blockers.fix: Queue and pace requests, and use bulk endpoints and webhooks to cut the number of calls.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The 429 status comes from third-party reports. Copper's page only states the limits.

blockers.cause: The token request lacks code, or was sent as JSON rather than form-encoded.
blockers.fix: Send application/x-www-form-urlencoded with grant_type, code, redirect_uri, client_id and client_secret.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: We observed this exact response from an empty POST to https://app.copper.com/oauth/token on 2026-10-20.

nuances.text: Copper says access tokens currently don't expire and don't need refreshing, and the flow returns no refresh token. Store tokens as long-lived secrets and handle revocation, because a leaked token stays valid until revoked.
There's a single scope, developer/v1/all, so your agent always gets read and write access to everything the user can see. Customers' security teams can't be offered read-only access.
Rate limits are 180 requests per minute for all API calls, plus 3 requests per second on bulk APIs. The docs don't say whether the limit is per user, per token or per account.
API keys are generated only by Copper Admins and are sent with three X-PW-* headers including the owner's email. They're a fallback for a single customer, not a scalable connection flow.
Copper has no OpenID Connect discovery document, so OAuth gives you API access, not Sign in with Copper. Fetch the current user via the API instead.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: https://app.copper.com/.well-known/openid-configuration returned 404 on 2026-10-20. The changelog notes a 'fetch current API user' endpoint added 2024-06-19.

nuances.text: The API moved to api.copper.com/developer_api/ in 2021. Older tutorials using api.prosperworks.com are out of date.
